chapter_title: Concerning the Three Images that are in the righte
spiritual_reading:
In the person who is being regenerated there are three distinct forms of reception and appearance.

The first is the inmost form in which wisdom from the Divine forms a new will and a new understanding; this new human is introduced by higher illumination, and it abides as an interior presence.

The second is an intermediate form: what remains and persists from the new human as it is held within the natural self. In that middle degree the renewed things are still bound within the hereditary selfhood and its habits, because this level has been formed through earlier states in which the natural self ruled.

The third is the outermost form that is added beneath them, in which life is expressed in the lowest degree through outward acts and sensory appearance.

These three forms act together as one process, though the text’s sequence here is partly broken. As the person is sustained by what is received from without, the life in him is alternately raised toward the inmost and lowered toward the outermost according to how reception is made. When it is lowered into the lowest form, the outermost strips away what does not belong to the person’s proper spiritual life and transfers what can be reordered into the intermediate form. Then again the life is raised and lowered in turn; and in this movement it casts off the intermediate impurities that cling from hostile influences—especially the excitations that inflame contentiousness. Disordered craving also clings and is carried along until it too is separated.

After this, a pure leading perception from higher illumination approaches and discloses the inmost form that is present, the new human. That guiding illumination goes before, elevating what can be elevated into higher states, and it is received into the inmost form. It gives the new human determinate shape and orders it with what is renewed within. The renewal is confirmed and fully organized by all the powers of that illumination which is present and makes its dwelling within the new human.

In this way the living power in a person is purified and truly lives, even as it enters the life of one who is being made righteous from without through the continual reception of what sustains the mind in varied ways. The living soul is to be wholly cleansed each day, and to pass through these three forms of life in order.

Thus it casts off the outermost selfhood that is not truly its own in the lowest degree. It also casts off the foreign life-admixtures that are not its own, which are mingled in the intermediate degree: irritations, cravings, dullness of mind, empty thinking, jealousy, contention, and the like, together with the false teachings that do not originate from the new life.

But in the inmost form itself it lives, and it is conjoined with patient endurance, with the completeness of faith, and with love which governs all things in right order. This governing illumination is what invests the new human with living truth, and it is called the turning-point at which life begins. It is first in the work of renewal, and it is also last, because it is the beginning within every stage and the final confirmation of the whole.

fills.fill: is being preserved in the flesh
fills.notes: The intermediate degree is described as the remainder of the new human held within the natural; correspondentially it is ‘kept’ or ‘preserved’ under the constraint of the fleshly level. This also matches the causal clause that follows: it is bound “as the old man” because earlier states formed it.
These three images are not three unrelated things but three discrete degrees acting as one process; thus the verb must express coordinated functioning.
The motion described is the alternation of raising and lowering according to reception; ‘elevated’ matches the spiritual translation’s ‘raised toward the inmost’.
The elevation is into the spiritual image; the next clause gives the contrary motion ‘down to the corporeal image’, so this must be the upward terminus.
The corporeal level strips off what is not proper and places what can be reordered into the intermediate degree; that recipient is the psychic image.
Marks the cycle described in the spiritual translation: after transfer into the intermediate, the movement repeats (‘then again it rises up and falls’).

The repeated falling is between degrees; here the text says it “falls to the … image” right before divesting “the psychical of the enemies”, so the target degree is again the psychic image where such admixtures are present.
Hostile admixtures in the middle degree are especially the excitations that kindle contentious states; correspondentially this is ‘stirring’ and ‘inflaming’.

fills.fill: also clings and is carried along
fills.notes: The spiritual translation requires that disordered craving remains attached through the process until separated; thus it ‘clings’ and is ‘borne with it’.

The list that follows begins with anger and desire; the correspondential sense specifies these as the notable excitations in the intermediate degree, so the phrase should introduce them as the chief instances within that level.

The series ‘anger and desire and …-ness and foolishness’ needs a state of obscuration in the natural mind that pairs with foolishness; ‘dull-ness’ fits the correspondential idea of torpor and loss of spiritual perception.

assessment: Most lacunae are either trivial letter-restorations or are tightly constrained by the correspondential sequence of discrete degrees (spiritual, psychic, corporeal) and the cyclic raising and lowering described in the provided spiritual translation. The most uncertain points are the exact verbs in ¶6 for coordinated operation and the precise idiom for the hostile excitations; these were restored to match the required spiritual mechanics (elevation, descent, stripping, transfer, repeated alternation) in an impersonal cosmological register.
